references.text: Abraham buys the field at Machpelah near Mamre from Ephron the Hittite, which includes the cave, to use it as a burial place for his family.
Isaac and Ishmael bury their father Abraham in the cave at the field of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought.
Jacob's sons bury him in the cave at the field of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought as a family burial site.
Creates a theological arc by showing that the cave was Abraham's burial place from Sarah until the time of Jacob.
Provides the legal and historical background for the property rights that make the burial possible.
Confirms that the property was permanently purchased and used by all of Abraham's household.
Establishes the status of the cave as a permanent and lawful burial site for Abraham's descendants.
Reveals the original intention to secure a permanent burial place for the family.
